title: ESM Live Binding vs CJS Value Copy Simulator
subtopicTitle: Module Systems: ESM vs CommonJS & Circular Dependencies
concept: Live Reference Bindings vs Copied Primitive Values
problemStatement: Implement `createLiveBindingStore()` that demonstrates the fundamental difference between ESM live bindings (which reflect exported counter changes when incremented) and CJS value copies (which remain frozen at the initial value).
interviewTrap: Candidates often assume ESM exports work like objects with values. In reality, ESM generates pointer references in the module record, so mutating the internal variable changes what importers see without re-exporting.

testCases.name: Both start at initial value 0
testCases.testFn: const store = createLiveBindingStore(); return store.getCjsCounter() + ':' + store.getEsmCounter();

testCases.name: After increment, CJS stays 0 while ESM updates to 1
testCases.testFn: const store = createLiveBindingStore(); store.increment(); return { cjs: store.getCjsCounter(), esm: store.getEsmCounter() };

testCases.name: Multiple increments continue updating ESM counter live
testCases.testFn: const store = createLiveBindingStore(); store.increment(); store.increment(); store.increment(); return store.getEsmCounter();

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: CommonJS exports are evaluated at runtime and copied by value into a module.exports object. ESM exports are live references bound during static analysis, meaning changes in the exporter reflect immediately in the importer.

3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the critical difference between CommonJS exports and ESM live bindings?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: CommonJS copies values: when a module exports a primitive (`let count = 0; module.exports = count`), the consumer receives a static COPY of `0`. Mutating `count` inside the module later does NOT update the consumer's variable. In ESM, `export let count = 0` creates a **Live Binding** (a reference into the module's lexical environment): when the exporter increments `count++`, consumers immediately see the updated value!
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The definitive technical difference between CJS and ESM.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Can an importer reassign an imported ESM variable?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: NO! Imported identifiers are **read-only views**. Attempting to write `import { count } from './m'; count = 5;` throws a compile-time/runtime `TypeError: Assignment to constant variable`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Verifies knowledge of ESM import immutability.

realWorldUseCases.description: Because ESM imports are static and declarative, bundlers construct static dependency graphs and eliminate dead exported code (tree-shaking), which is impossible with dynamic CommonJS requires.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: import { usedFn } from './utils'; // unusedFn is pruned from bundle

howToExplain.opening: ECMAScript Modules (ESM) use static live bindings where imported variables are dynamic, read-only references to the exporter's lexical environment.
keyPoints: CommonJS copies values; ESM creates live reference bindings.
Mutations inside the exporting module are reflected in real time across all importers.
Imports are strictly read-only for consumers.
Static structure enables dead-code elimination (tree-shaking) during bundling.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Live bindings allow circular dependencies and real-time state synchronization to work seamlessly in modern JavaScript.
analogies: CommonJS is printing a balance on a paper receipt (static snapshot); ESM is looking at your live banking app (live binding updates automatically).

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming ESM imports can be conditionally declared inside if statements.
commonMistakes.why: Static import statements must be top-level. Dynamic imports must use `import()` returning a Promise.
commonMistakes.correct: Use static imports at file top, or `await import('./module')` for dynamic loading.

followUpDeepDive.question: What are the three phases of ESM module loading in ECMA-262?
followUpDeepDive.answer: 1) Construction: parse files, build Module Graph. 2) Instantiation: allocate memory slots for live bindings (linking exports to imports). 3) Evaluation: execute code to populate those slots.
